title: RAISING UP THE TABERNACLE OF DAVID THAT FELL

sense.text:
“Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth”: the wicked man here is the white man. “Though he hide it under his tongue”: he hid the evil speech for about sixty years, from the civil rights days until now. Now he says the time is up, we are tired of feeling bad, we are not humbling ourselves to you any more, we are going to tell you exactly how we feel. They call it black fatigue.

This is read with Ecclesiasticus 12:10 to show the new people that the Bible says the same thing as the Apocrypha. People think the Apocrypha says something totally different; it does not.
“Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth”: he never let it go. The wickedness was still there the whole time, kept in his mouth, waiting.

precepts.why:
Ecclesiasticus gives a name to the wicked man of Job 20: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” It tells you plainly he is your enemy. But to understand it you must be able to identify who the enemy is. Black people call each other the enemy; they will never look at their oppressor and say, that white man enslaved us, that is the enemy.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”: though he is nice to you. The white man gave you a raise, a good one; that means nothing, they had a budget. He is nice to you today. Affirmative action, and then they get rid of that too, thanks to Clarence Thomas, who became a judge by affirmative action and then ended it. They smile with that plastic smile in your face.

“thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass”: like a glass covered with dust or mist that you wipe, and now you can see through it. “and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away”: now you can see the wickedness of verse 10 is still with him, the same wickedness Job says he kept still within his mouth.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place”: that is what we did. When we fought the Muslims, the black Jews and Christians went to the Caucasus Mountains and said we need the help of the Khazars, the wildlings, and they converted to Judaism and joined our army. We set them by us, all through our military. Now he is the Jew and you are the Gentile; he is the Christian and you are the Gentile. Othello, the last of the Moors in Spain, whose Edomite friends were plotting to kill him and drive all black people out of Spain, shows the same thing.

“neither let him sit at thy right hand, lest he seek to take thy seat”: we made that mistake. When black people go into business with white folks, somehow the white man takes it over. An Edomite's steakhouse was getting no business until an old black man made it boom, and the white man took the success. Don't trust these white folks, even when you say, he's different, he's not like the rest.

“and thou at the last remember my words, and be pricked therewith”: when they put your teeth on the curb and stomp them out, as in American History X, then you will remember God's words.

sense.text: “even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”: Peter is addressing Paul's writings. Peter read all the letters Paul wrote. The Most High had Paul write it difficult for a reason.

“in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”: if you are unlearned and unstable, you struggle and wrestle with Paul's writings, “as they do also the other scriptures”, the Old Testament scriptures, “unto their own destruction.”

That is how replacement theology, supersessionism, took hold: the Christian doctrine that the church has replaced national Israel as God's chosen people, so that the covenants and promises made to Israel are said to be spiritually transferred to the church, the church being called the new Israel. It came up around the time of the Pope and the Catholics, around the time of slavery. That is why, when you ask them where the twelve tribes of Israel are in the New Testament, they never have an answer. They say all the prophecies in the Old Testament about Israel are really about the Christian church today, and black and Latino people believe those lies.

“I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah”: there was a split, which is why he separates us like that. Christians avoid this verse, because when you ask who the new covenant is for, it tells you crystal clear.

“Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers”: he gave us animal sacrifice; that was the old covenant. “although I was an husband unto them”: the twelve tribes are the bride and God is the husband.

“I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts”: this is the kingdom it is talking about, when “they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord.”

“Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night”: this is the answer to replacement theology, the answer to supersessionism. “If those ordinances depart from before me”, if you can destroy the sun, the moon and the stars, “then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.”

So the twelve tribes of Israel are still here to this day. Even in the time of Paul the twelve tribes were there, yet Christians cannot point them out in the New Testament; they say nobody knows where they are, they are lost, because everything is the church. It is a lie.

“If heaven above can be measured”: the galaxies out there, nobody knows them. “and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath”, which nobody can do yet, “I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done”. Nobody can measure heaven or search out all the places of the earth, so the twelve tribes cannot be cast off. This is where Paul was getting it from.

precepts.why:
Paul quotes Jeremiah 31:31 in Hebrews: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. Ask a Christian who the new covenant is for, and it tells you right there.

“Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt”: not according to the covenant that involved animal sacrifice. “because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not”: he regarded us not, meaning we went into slavery.

“For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days”: Israel there means all twelve tribes. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: this is the kingdom. So Paul wrote Hebrews taking it straight from Jeremiah.

Paul tells Timothy, “when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.” The books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah, Micah: the books of the Bible, not books on how to braid your hair or tie your shoes. Parchments are writing papers.

So Paul read the Old Testament books and based his epistles on those writings. That is why Hebrews 8 says what Jeremiah 31 says: Jeremiah is where Paul got it from.

“Considerest thou not what this people have spoken, saying, The two families which the Lord hath chosen, he hath even cast them off?” The two families are Judah and Israel; remember the split among the twelve tribes. That was the thought even then: God has destroyed the two kingdoms, God has destroyed the twelve tribes of Israel. “thus they have despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them”: that is supersessionism, replacement theology, already back then.

“If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth; Then will I cast away the seed of Jacob”: day and night are still here, the ordinances of heaven and earth are still here, and then and only then will he cast away the seed of Jacob. Just as in Jeremiah 31:36-37.

“and David my servant, so that I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”: out of that seed comes Christ. If Israel were cast away there would be no need for Christ; but Christ did come, which means the twelve tribes are still here today.

“for I will cause their captivity to return, and have mercy on them”: he is going to bring us back to the land out of this misery. It does not mean he will put us back in slavery; he calls us the captivity many times in the Bible. Return where? To our homeland, with mercy.

sense.text:
Paul could easily have said Judah and Israel, as he did in Hebrews and in Romans 9, but in many of his epistles he uses other words for the twelve tribes. “For whom he did foreknow”: foreknow means knew from the past. Christians say that means everybody, the church. Stress that word on the street; they are so brainwashed with replacement theology.

“he also did predestinate”: they love to say there is no such thing in the Bible as predestination. There is, for the twelve tribes of Israel. We were his people in the past, we are his people today and for evermore; that will not change. We are predestined to be his chosen forever. Whether we as individuals make it is up to each one: you might decide to be a private dancer, an escort, a homo, and you will be gone.

“to be conformed to the image of his Son”: he is going to transform the twelve tribes into the image of his Son, Christ, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

“Moreover whom he did predestinate”: chosen from the beginning of time; this is my people forever. “them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified”: it is not everybody who is called and justified. The only ones called and justified are Israel.

precepts.why:
Who did God know from the past? “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. So it is not everybody; there is no church he is talking about, no Presbyterian, no Catholic. “therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”: and we were punished.

That is whom he did foreknow in Romans 8:29.

“In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified”. The only ones being justified are all the seed of Israel: not the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, not all those false religions. That is who Romans 8:30 says he justified.

“Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called”. He is not calling all the nations on planet earth, not Catholics, not Jehovah's Witnesses, not Baptists. He is only calling Israel.

All of that goes back to replacement theology, which came about in the Catholic church and was carried on by the Protestant church many of us grew up in, teaching that all the scriptures you read are the church now.

sense.text: Before you get to Ephesians 2, where Christians try to hem you up, you have to deal with Ephesians 1:1. “to the saints which are at Ephesus”: who are the saints Paul is addressing? The children of Israel only.

“who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ”: that is heavy, and a whole class could be spent on it, on power, knowledge, wisdom and understanding, but that is for another class.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”: that is predestination. He chose us before the earth was made. Stay right there with a Christian and he won't understand it.

“that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”: that is difficult for blacks and Latinos. We are a ratchet race of people. When the white man talks about us, I don't get mad, I chuckle: who is fighting on the Carnival cruise boats, who is twerking on cop cars? A black man opens a restaurant for black people to eat good food and relax, and here comes a black woman twerking on the furniture, and when he asks her to get off they shut that brother down. We have whole tendencies. So when God says he wants us to be holy, we must study the law and apply the law.
“Having predestinated us”: there it is again, predestinated before the foundation of the world, “unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself”.

“wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved. In whom we have redemption through his blood”: we, the saints, have redemption through the blood of Christ, “the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.”

precepts.why:
“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The only saints are the children of Israel. There are no saints called Catholics, Baptists, Methodists or Presbyterians; that is supersessionism, replacement theology.

So the saints which are at Ephesus, to whom Paul writes, are the children of Israel.

“O ye seed of Israel his servant, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.” We are the chosen ones. That is the us of “he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”.

You can mess a Christian's head up with this. Tell him: you don't know the Bible, we know the Bible; just sit there, listen and learn.

“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” So for us to be the holy people God destines us to be, “that we should be holy and without blame before him”, we must study the law and apply the law.

And no, Christians, we are not talking about animal sacrifice. We are talking about the laws of morality, laws of civility, laws of ceremony and laws of diet. That is holy.

sense.text: Replacement theology says the church has taken the twelve tribes of Israel out: you are no more. Paul had to address that same issue. “Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no. God has not cast away the twelve tribes of Israel. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” On the street, that first verse tells you what the subject is.
“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” There is that word again, foreknew. Paul deals with it right here, the same as Amos 3:2.

Elijah thought he was by himself: “I am left alone, and they seek my life.” But God answered, “I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal”: men who did not worship idols.
“Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.” The election of grace deals with the twelve tribes of Israel.

“And if by grace, then is it no more of works”: a Christian will try to hem you up with that, saying it is not about works, my brother. Christians assume that when Paul uses the word works, he means thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. That is not what Paul is talking about at all. The works are the works of the temple, the works of animal sacrifice, the offerings and things of that nature. “otherwise grace is no more grace.”

precepts.why:
When they argue with you over Romans 11:1, jump down to verse 26: “And so all Israel shall be saved”. And so means as a result of all Paul said: all twelve tribes shall be saved.

“There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.” Unto them who? The twelve tribes of Israel. So God has not cast away his people.

“For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” We are the elect. Israel is the elect, not all nations.

This is where Paul gets the remnant according to the election of grace.

This shows what the works are: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.” The reader must stress it: all the work of the house of our God.

Those are the works Paul means in Romans 11:6: the work of the temple, the animal sacrifices and offerings. Not the commandments.

sense.text: “Woe to them that are at ease in Zion”: woe to our people at ease in Jerusalem, the southern kingdom. “and trust in the mountain of Samaria”: that is the northern kingdom. Both kingdoms are named here.

Calneh, Hamath the great, and Gath of the Philistines are lands over there. He compares Zion and Samaria with those kingdoms: “be they better than these kingdoms? or their border greater than your border?”

“That lie upon beds of ivory”: the rich. “and invent to themselves instruments of musick, like David”: they were creating their own instruments of music. “but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph”: the affliction of Joseph was the destruction of the northern kingdom, when Assyria came to take them.
“Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive”: the first to go were their kings.

“I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces”: all twelve tribes were going. “therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein”: Judah, the southern kingdom, was going to get it, and the northern kingdom too.

precepts.why:
This explains Zion: Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes “unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.” So Jerusalem was also called Zion.

That is why at ease in Zion in Amos 6:1 is the southern kingdom, and the mountain of Samaria is the northern kingdom.

Christ speaks with the Samaritan woman, and she says, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”, which was Mount Gerizim, “and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” He is in Samaria, and she is saying, you Jews say Jerusalem. The two mountains of Amos 6:1 are here: Samaria and Zion.

“Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Why? Because 70 AD was coming, and Rome was going to destroy the remaining Israelites. “Ye worship ye know not what”: you of the northern kingdom do not understand what you worship, because the northern kingdom went into idolatry. “we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews”: salvation comes from Judah.

“the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”. He was letting her know the temple was going to be destroyed and the Israelites would go into captivity; you will have to run for your lives and deal with the Lord one on one. No more priests intervening for you. So what Amos prophesied about Zion and Samaria, Christ said too.
“In Judah is God known”. That is why Christ came out of Judah, and why salvation is of the Jews: salvation comes from Judah. He was not tribe hopping.

sense.text: “the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand”: a plumb line is used for measuring; he is going to do some measuring. “I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more”: I am going to cut them off.

“the high places of Isaac shall be desolate”: that is the southern kingdom. “and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste”: the northern kingdom. “and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword”: the northern kingdom.

Amaziah the priest of Beth-el complains to Jeroboam: “the land is not able to bear all his words.” The land can't take the prophecies of Amos, saying God is going to do this and that to us. Amos was telling the northern kingdom they were going into slavery soon: “Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.”

“flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there”: get out of here and go talk to Judah. That is what the northern kingdom told Amos: we don't want to hear that. “But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king's chapel, and it is the king's court.” Don't prophesy over here; we are the northern kingdom; shut your black lips.

“Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn?” They could not stand it when the holy days came; they wanted to do business, buying and selling. People ask how we know we cannot buy and sell on a new moon: right here. “and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?” They wanted to mess with the measurements. This is what Israel wanted to do.
“That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes”: they wanted to buy the poor Israelites. You see how bad it was.
“and it shall be cast out and drowned, as by the flood of Egypt”: the same way Egypt destroyed us, he would have Assyria do the same to them.

“I will cause the sun to go down at noon”, “I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation”. Judgment was coming on all twelve tribes, but it started with the northern kingdom.

“the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”: he said he would get Judah and the northern kingdom, starting with the northern kingdom. He calls us the sinful kingdom; let's talk about wicked Israel. “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob”: although I will wipe you out, I will not destroy all the Israelites. The northern kingdom would be taken out of the land and the southern kingdom would be taken out of the land.

Here is the proof: “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Once he got all of us out of the land, we were sifted everywhere, amongst all nations. “yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth”: the least of us will not be lost.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” That is just like Christianity: nothing is going to happen to us, we're good in white Jesus' name.

Notice the order: Israel destroyed in verse 8, sifted and scattered in verse 9, the sinners die in verse 10, and then “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”. He is already telling us God's plan and purpose, because we are predestined; he foreknew us from before the foundation of the earth.

The tabernacle of David fell when the twelve tribes were split into two kingdoms. “and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”: he is going to rebuild the whole thing as in the days of old.

precepts.why:
If you choose to use the sinful kingdom for America, here is the precept: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” The great city is Babylon the great, and spiritually is the key word to highlight.

It is not the real Sodom or the real Egypt, but a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt. Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, so this is not the real Jerusalem either; America is a spiritual Jerusalem. Just as they hated Christ in the real Jerusalem, they hate the true Christ and his teachings here.

sense.text: To understand what happened to the tabernacle of David, go just before Amos. “the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their gods: Chemosh, Ishtar of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice, some involved sexual orgies; however far your mind can go, Solomon went there. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods. He “had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.”
“I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant”: I am going to take the twelve tribes of Israel from you.

“Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father's sake”: the only reason it would not happen in Solomon's days was the promise God made to King David. “but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son”: Rehoboam.
“Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake which I have chosen.”

precepts.why:
Solomon says it himself: “I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly”. Folly means all kinds of sin. “I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.”

So when Solomon got old he did a lot of evil, and that is why the Lord was angry with him. And yes, he did repent, as you read in Ecclesiastes 12.

sense.text: “And the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valour”: the same Jeroboam read of in Amos. Solomon, “seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph”: Solomon put Jeroboam over the house of Joseph, over Ephraim. Jeroboam is the servant God said he would give the kingdom to.

The prophet Ahijah found Jeroboam clad in a new garment, “And Ahijah caught the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces”. Imagine having on a new garment and somebody starts ripping pieces off.
“Take thee ten pieces”, “and will give ten tribes to thee”: that is the northern kingdom. “But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake”.

To understand the New Testament you should be fully aware of what happened to the twelve tribes. Rehoboam is Solomon's son. Jeroboam had fled into Egypt because Solomon was angry with him, knowing he would get the kingdom, and wanted to kill him.

“Thy father made our yoke grievous”: the holy temple had its tribute, but when Solomon built those houses of worship for his wives he forced Israel to pay tribute to those gods. Israel was saying, take away all those taxes he put on us for those false gods, make it “lighter, and we will serve thee.”

Rehoboam first consulted the old men who stood before Solomon, his father's counsel. They said, “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.”

“But he forsook the counsel of the old men”: he did not want to listen to his father's old friends who had knowledge, wisdom and experience, and “consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”, his peers.

See the difference: to the old men he said, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men he said, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”: we, all of us together; you are my peers, we are running this thing.
“My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins.” “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions”: I will be worse than my father.

“And the king answered the people roughly”, after the counsel of his friends. Notice they show you the character of Solomon in his old age: “my father also chastised you with whips”. When people did not want to pay those taxes, he sent men out to force them.
“for the cause was from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam”.
“What portion have we in David?” “to your tents, O Israel”: that is spoken to the ten tribes. “now see to thine own house, David”: see to your own house, Judah.

Rehoboam reigned over the children of Israel in the cities of Judah. He sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, “and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died”: you came to collect money, we are not giving you anything. And Rehoboam got out of there to Jerusalem, knowing they would kill him next.
“So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.” That is the fall of the tabernacle of David.

precepts.why:
This is how young men should deal with their father's friends. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son will look after his father's friends. Rehoboam should have honoured Solomon's old men, his father's friends, and he did not.

Some in this congregation make the same mistake Rehoboam made. “Not a novice”: a novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte, “lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” He thinks, I know all the precepts.

His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that spirit destroys itself. That is who Rehoboam looked to when he forsook the old men and took counsel with the young men.

There have been brothers among us who felt that to be a leader you have to lead men by being rough and filled with pride. “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.”

Rule people with roughness and pride and you will lose your position. We had a case like that in Cali, and many over here in the States, in New York, Texas and other places: brothers who thought that to lead a sanctuary they had to rule the people with roughness and pride, taking advantage of the brothers and sisters. They had to be removed. Rehoboam answered the people roughly and lost ten tribes.

sense.text: “And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance”. Notice they call Ephraim and Manasseh strangers. Some of the northern kingdom loved the Lord and went with the kingdom of Judah. Kings and Chronicles always each give a little something the other does not. This one is very important on the street.

“In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria”, took the cities of Galilee and all the land of Naphtali, “and carried them captive to Assyria.” This is what was read in the book of Amos: what Amos told them was coming.

Rehoboam had Judah and Benjamin on his side, “And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts.” The Levites were scattered throughout all twelve tribes. Those who lived in the kingdom of Judah were fine, but not those in the northern kingdom, because at the high holy days, especially the three top feasts, Levi's job was to tell everybody we have to go up to Jerusalem to worship. Remember the woman of Samaria: you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship. That is what Levi was doing back then.

“for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto the Lord”: they kicked Levi out. We don't want you here trying to get us to do what God says; we want to worship idols. And Jeroboam “ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.”

“And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem”. The whole northern kingdom was not idolatrous; a remnant joined with the southern kingdom, like Tobit. That is why 2 Chronicles 15:9 shows Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon falling to Judah.

We are discussing the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and explaining what happened. “the Lord was very angry with Israel”, the ten tribes, “and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only”, meaning the southern kingdom.

“Also Judah kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made”: Judah was doing the same thing the northern kingdom was doing. “And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel”: God was angry at all twelve tribes now.

“For he rent Israel from the house of David”, “and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.” They did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam “Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets.” That is what Amos was telling them would happen. They did not want to hear it, but it happened.
The king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath and Sepharvaim “and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”.

If you are reading your four chapters a day you should already know this history. There were two kings: Hezekiah of Judah and Hoshea of Israel. Shalmaneser king of Assyria besieged Samaria, and at the end of three years “Samaria was taken.”

“the king of Assyria did carry away Israel unto Assyria”, “Because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord their God, but transgressed his covenant, and all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and would not hear them, nor do them.”

Now what happened with Judah. In the days of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar came up, “and Jehoiakim became his servant three years: then he turned and rebelled against him.” He was set up in authority and was supposed to pay tribute and obey Nebuchadnezzar, and he rebelled.

The Lord sent bands of the Chaldees, Syrians, Moabites and Ammonites “against Judah to destroy it”, “to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh”. Now Judah was being removed out of the Lord's sight. King Manasseh was an evil brother, but he did repent.
“for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the Lord would not pardon.” So both kingdoms went into captivity: the Assyrian captivity and the Babylonian captivity.

What has been read ties in with the first chapter of Matthew. “all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations”: from Abraham to David we had the kingdom, and before it, as God told Abraham his seed would, we went into the Egyptian captivity. “and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations”: the split, the sin, the northern kingdom into the Assyrian captivity, then Babylon took all. “and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations”: for our sins we had the Babylonian captivity, then the Persian, then the Greek, and we were under Rome until Christ was born.

It matters a lot. The first chapter of Matthew is telling you Israel was in captivity. On the street this verse speaks volumes.

“and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” We went into slavery because of our sins. That is why we needed a Saviour; all the other nations know we needed a Saviour.

During the Persian captivity we got liberty. “the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus said, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.” He said that because he knew it was a prophecy. The writings of Flavius Josephus give more detail on how the prophets showed Cyrus what he must do, and he obeyed.
“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem”: he makes the proclamation to all twelve tribes, not just Judah.

We were in Babylon seventy years, and before that the northern kingdom was already out there. Cyrus gives the Israelites liberty, but if you decide you don't want to go back to the land of Israel, and want to stay where you have lived for decades, “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. So some of the northern kingdom went back with the kingdom of Judah, and some of the southern kingdom stayed out there with the northern kingdom. Everybody did not go back.

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls Cyrus his anointed: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

This was written about 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. When he came of age he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew the God of Israel was dealing with him to release his people. That is why he said the Lord God of heaven had given him all the kingdoms of the earth.

sense.text: This is the same Ezra, written Esdras, the Greek form of his name. “Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”: what was read earlier in 2 Kings. “and he carried them over the waters”: to be carried over the waters, you have to be on ships. The ten tribes went into captivity on ships.

“But they took this counsel among themselves”: this was during the time of Cyrus, when he gave them liberty, around 529 BC. “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”: highlight that on the street. There is a new claim that before the American Indians other races were already living here. Stop the lies.
“That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.”

“And they entered into Euphrates by the narrow passages of the river”, as the red line on the map shows. “For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.”

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”: travelling a year and a half, men, women and children, they had to stop for victuals and supplies. That is why it is important to know this history. “and the same region is called Arsareth.” The map shows Arsareth at the top. The entry on Arsareth by Morris Jastrow Jr. and Kaufmann Kohler calls it the land beyond the great river, far away from the habitation of man, in which the ten tribes of Israel dwell, observing the laws of Moses until the time of restoration, according to 2 Esdras 13:45; and it says Columbus identified America with this land.

Some Israelites came back to the land. Now watch what they were calling some of the kingdom of Israel: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. They were calling them Gentiles.
“The people which sat in darkness saw great light”: this comes from Isaiah 9.
“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ was that great light spoken of.

precepts.why:
This is the prophecy Isaiah wrote: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” That is the Assyrian captivity.

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”. Isaiah prophesied it, and Matthew reveals what it is really talking about: when Christ came preaching, he was the light to Zebulun and Naphtali, Galilee of the Gentiles.

“and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles; To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.”

Those Gentiles are not talking about other nations. It all goes back to Matthew 4:15-16: Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern kingdom, the people that sat in darkness.

sense.text: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: those Gentiles are the northern kingdom. That is why they are in the same sentence with Samaria. Why does he name the Samaritans? That was the leading tribe, Ephraim. Don't go to them yet.
“But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: the kingdom of Judah. Start with Judah first.
“And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

precepts.why:
Where do we get Judah first? Here is the prophecy: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

When Christ came he was not just gathering all Israel; he said, I have to start with Judah, and the rest come later on. That is why he sent the twelve to the lost sheep first.

sense.text: After the disciples dealt with Judah, what did Christ do? “Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples”: Christ never baptized anybody in water; his disciples did.
He left Judea for Galilee, “And he must needs go through Samaria.” Remember he had said, don't go to the Gentiles and the Samaritans.
“Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey”: he was tired.

“How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The southern kingdom did not deal with the northern kingdom. Remember the rift from Rehoboam; that was always the problem. She reminds him, you Jews don't deal with us.

“Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”: right there she tells you she is an Israelite. People on YouTube say she is not, because the king of Assyria put men of Babylon in the land of Samaria. But there is more history; that is why Ezra 1 was read, where Israelites came back to the land.

“Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again”. If the woman was lying about her identity, why didn't Christ correct her? Further down he does correct her about something, but not about her nationality. He goes on with the conversation: “the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

“For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband”. He knows what she is doing, so wouldn't he have corrected her in verse 12 if she were lying that Jacob was her father? He lets her know she is living a whorish lifestyle: the man she is having sex with is not her husband. Sex does not constitute marriage.
“Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”: Mount Gerizim in Samaria. Note Joshua 8:32 for that mountain.

“the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”: the hour is 70 AD. Nobody would be worshipping in Jerusalem or Samaria. Amos said the same thing, that Zion and Samaria would be wiped out.
“for salvation is of the Jews”: salvation is of Judah. “the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”: because the temple was going to be destroyed soon.

“I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ”: Messiah is Hebrew; Christ is Greek; it means anointed. “I that speak unto thee am he.” If she was not an Israelite, why would he reveal himself to her as the Messiah she knew would come?
His disciples “marvelled that he talked with the woman”, because the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. They were asking, why is he talking to this Samaritan?

“And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him”, and “he abode there two days.” If they were not Israelites, why would he stay and teach them two days? It makes no sense. “for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world”: the Saviour of the world of Israel.

precepts.why:
“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Jeroboam set up priests in the land, as the history showed, so Judah did not deal with them.

That is why the woman of Samaria says the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
“And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”: Samaria was the capital of Ephraim. Christ is in Samaria talking to a Samaritan woman, an Ephraimite, which is why she can say “our father Jacob”.

sense.text: Christ went to the Samaritans; in Matthew 10 he said don't go to them yet, because Judah had to get it first. “There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band”. Write this down: Cesarea is in the land of Israel, in the land of Manasseh, west Manasseh, right beside Samaria. That is where Cornelius comes from. Peter lived in Joppa, the seaport, and sailed up to visit him; Christ was raised further up in Galilee, so Cornelius would have got word of the teaching in that area. Nearby is Scythopolis, the city of the Scythians, where northern kingdom Israelites lived; Paul wrote of the Scythians in Colossians.

“A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” People say he was another nation but devout. We used to read it that way too. Then how was he a devout man according to the law? How did he fear God and know how to pray to God without knowing the law? So yes, Cornelius is an Israelite of the northern kingdom.
“Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” Now the Lord is dealing with him.
“send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter”: the deacon showed where Peter lived, in Joppa.

“Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour”: noon, the noonday prayer; we pray evening, morning and noon. Bishop Kani went into a great breakdown of this vision, slow and excellent, in the class he and the Bishop did, Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common.

“a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”, with all manner of beasts, and “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” Peter said he had never eaten any thing common or unclean.
“What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” What has God cleansed? Does he cleanse Esau? Never read that one. He cleanses the twelve tribes.

Peter breaks down the dream: “it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”: remember Ezekiel 37:22, they shall be no more two nations. “but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man: it is not about roaches or ants or eating the unclean pig. The vision was about man: the Israelites being cleansed, the northern kingdom being cleansed.

This is where Christians get you: “God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” They say Cornelius was a white man, an Italian, a Roman, accepted from every nation. That is replacement theology, supersessionism.
The next verse explains Cornelius: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”. Acts 10 tells you this was for the children of Israel.

precepts.why:
Before Acts 10, see how the disciples kept it: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

That goes back to Matthew 10:5-6. They were still dealing with the kingdom of Judah only, and not with the other Israelites, until God showed Peter the vision about Cornelius.
“There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cesarea”: the same place Cornelius is from. There were disciples who came from Cesarea as well.

How do you become a devout man? “And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there”. You are devout according to the law, and the other nations did not have the law.

So when Acts 10:2 calls Cornelius devout and one that feared God, it means he knew the law: an Israelite.

The certain vessel in Peter's vision goes with this: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

The vessel let down with all manner of beasts is Israel, swallowed up among the Gentiles.

What has God cleansed? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel”, “and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. That goes back to everything read today.

“but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” God says he is going to cleanse us, the twelve tribes. That is “What God hath cleansed”, and why Peter was not to call Cornelius common.

sense.text: Acts 10 made it official. Christ showed them in John 4, but the disciples never went to the northern kingdom; they left it alone until God showed Peter the vision. Now in Acts 13, “when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul”.

“It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”: the reader has to stress first. You who? The Jews, the kingdom of Judah. “but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.”
“I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth.”

precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. That is why Paul says it was necessary that the word should first be spoken to the Jews: Judah gets the gospel first, and the others after.

The Christian who asked Captain Osee on the Cassandra Show why we once taught only black Americans and now say Hispanics and Latinos are Israelites too has his answer here: I will save Judah first. It has always been that way.
“Galilee of the Gentiles”: those Gentiles are the northern kingdom. So when Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles, and the light of the Gentiles, it is the same Gentiles: Zebulun and Naphtali.

Paul did what Christ did when he walked the earth: “After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.” He was not walking with the southern kingdom any more.

Galilee is Zebulun and Naphtali, as Matthew 4:15 showed. The Jews rejected Christ and said, you are no Saviour, you cannot forgive sins, so he went to the Gentiles; and Paul and Barnabas met the same rejection from the Jews and turned to the Gentiles. Hold those precepts on deck.

sense.text: When you hear us teaching, we always speak about context. You cannot assume that because it says Gentiles it means the other nations. The Zondervan Bible dictionary says it usually means a non-Israelite people, not always; there are times when Gentiles refers to Israelites in a Gentile state of mind, because God cut them off from being his people in Hosea 1. Here “the way of the Gentiles” and “any city of the Samaritans” are the same thing.

Some will say verse 5 is the heathen and verse 6 is the Israelites. But “the lost sheep of the house of Israel” here is the southern kingdom, the house of Jacob, while the Gentiles and Samaritans of verse 5 are the house of Joseph.

precepts.why:
Obadiah shows the Samaritans, the Gentiles and Israel at the same time: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame”. The house of Jacob in Obadiah 18 is Judah alone, the southern kingdom: Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The house of Joseph is Ephraim and his fellows, the rest.

So Christ says the exact same thing in Matthew 10: don't go to the Samaritans or the Gentiles, that is the house of Joseph, but rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the house of Jacob, the southern kingdom.

sense.text:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” Before this, the teaching was primarily to the kingdom of Judah alone; then the Most High showed them about the other tribes, and the twelve tribes sign went up.

See that part, do not magnify themselves against Judah. The brother who was here, Archangel, an Ephraimite, gathered all the Ephraimites in the school and started his own little camp; and now the one called Cornelius in LA wants a Mexican camp. When he gathered them he started speaking evil against the ones who helped his wife and his family when he was down and out. There are northern kingdom people who hate Judah's guts: they sit among us, learn, praise the leaders, bide their time, and when they see the northern kingdom coming in they say, come with us. It is the same spirit as the split, when the northern kingdom said, we are not listening to them. That is why the scripture says the envy of Ephraim shall depart.

“And if some of the branches be broken off”: that is Judah broken off. “and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree”: the grafting in is the joining of the two sticks in Ezekiel 37.

“Boast not against the branches”: don't boast against Judah. “But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee”: the root is Christ. You are not bearing Christ; Christ is the one who keeps the northern kingdom grafted in with Judah.
“Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in”: the northern kingdom would say Judah fell off so the northern kingdom could come in.
“Well; because of unbelief they were broken off”: Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off, “and thou standest by faith”: northern kingdom, you stand by faith. “Be not highminded, but fear”.

precepts.why:
“The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

Judah is the green olive tree whose branches are broken: the branches broken off in Romans 11:17.

“take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.”

That is the grafting in of Romans 11:17: the northern kingdom joined to Judah into one stick.

Where did we read don't boast and don't be highminded? In Zechariah 12:7: “that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” That the northern kingdom do not magnify themselves against Judah.

So to magnify themselves is to be highminded and to boast against the branches. Romans 11 says the same thing Zechariah says.

sense.text: “I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”, saying “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” Don't let the war pop off to the max until the servants of God are sealed with the law of God in Christ.
“there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” These 144,000 are the leaders, the leading men.

Twelve thousand of every tribe, Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph and Benjamin. To be sealed they have to know who they are, at least to some extent; that is why the twelve tribes sign goes up even though people get mad at it. How can you read all the tribes here and be confused about the twelve tribes? Replacement theology says these are spiritual tribes. You can't make this stuff up.

precepts.why:
This is the precept for the winds: “there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”.

So the four winds held by the angels are their military, the multitude gathered from the four winds.
The seal of the living God: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of God are sealed with the law.

sense.text: “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.”
“Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”, as Revelation 21 shows. “Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” Other nations are not there; they are not mentioned here.
“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.”

“Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of you are busy praying for Haiti, for Puerto Rico, for Mexico, for America. The Bible says pray for Jerusalem. Jerusalem is a people before it is a place: we are Jerusalem. Pray for us; we are not supposed to be praying to stop the war over there. They have to be moved out of our land so we can go back home.

“Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces. For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee. Because of the house of the Lord our God I will seek thy good.”

precepts.why:
Why does it say Jerusalem is builded as a city compact together? Start at verse 12: it “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”. This is our book; the kingdom is ours.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs”: about 1,500 miles. “The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal”: like a square, like a box. That is compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits”, about 216 feet, approximately, “according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” So it is actually larger.
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”. These are the thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David, in Psalms 122:5.

“And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Those are the thrones of judgment of Psalms 122:5. Don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it.

They shall prosper that love Jerusalem: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

That is what to pray for: not for Haiti or Puerto Rico or America, but that Jerusalem be made a praise in the earth.

sense.text: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. We fell when there was the split and we went into slavery unto this day; now he is raising us up as in the days of old. We are coming back to who we are.

Acts 15 says the residue of men might seek after the Lord; Amos says the same thing in different words: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. This is what the tabernacle of David is going to do: possess the remnant of Edom and of all the other nations. Those called by my name are the ones who call themselves Jewish and call themselves Christians, for Christian means anointed one, and they are not the anointed one. “saith the Lord that doeth this.” We are going to have everybody in captivity.

In Acts it is written nicer, because in Rome's time they would read all the letters you carried; residue of men seeking after the Lord, they would not know what it meant. Phebe carried many of those letters.

precepts.why:
“Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth”: until Israel brought forth. “then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.” The remnant of Christ's brethren.

Why? Because we fell, and now he is raising us up as in the days of old.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”: teraphim are little images made of family members.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” That is I will build it as in the days of old. In these latter days David is going to be here. Who he is, we don't know.

“Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.” This is Christ. “Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us.”

“Turn us again, O God”: turn us again to your laws, to our identity, our nationality, “and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.” That is the raising up of the tabernacle of David.

Peter and them are talking about what happened with Cornelius, and Simeon quotes Amos 9:11: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. We fell down when there was the split and we went into slavery unto this day.

Why bring that up while talking about Cornelius? Because Cornelius was of the northern kingdom. It would make no sense to say this about Cornelius if he were not of the twelve tribes. God went to Cornelius to take out a people for his name: the northern kingdom, to bring them back, not the non-Israelite nations. That was the healer of the breach.

“and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”: God will build up the twelve tribes again. “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”: the other nations. “and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: write this down, the people that call themselves Jews and the people that call themselves Christians. The quote of Amos 9:11 is exact, and Amos 9:12 tells how the residue of men shall seek after the Lord: by Israel possessing the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” That is the Lord building again the tabernacle of David that is fallen.

As Israel grows, everything will be set up the way the scriptures say. Some say, let's just have a Mexican camp; but how many of them have come into this truth and repented so far? Say two hundred. Even with thousands of us, the numbers are still too small. When the numbers get astronomical, then we can say, you Ephraim, be with this tribe and teach and guide them; Benjamin, take that. Nobody is going to do any funky business. Many of the northern kingdom think they can skip over Judah, and that is not according to scripture: the Most High says Judah first. Brothers who think, I have learned enough, I figured out the secret sauce, now I want to be the boss, will pay the cost.

sense.text: “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek”: Christ is that ensign, and the Gentiles shall seek to Christ. This is a good scripture to explain the Gentiles, together with Matthew 4:15.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”, from Assyria, which is Turkey; from Egypt, in Africa; from Pathros, Sudan; from Cush, Ethiopia; from Elam, Iran and Pakistan; from Shinar, Iraq; from Hamath, Syria; and from the islands of the sea: Puerto Rico, Haiti, the Pacific islands.
“and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” Notice what he calls the Gentiles: the outcasts of Israel.

“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart”: nobody is going to be saved with a hateful spirit for his brother. “and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off”: the other nations. “Ephraim shall not envy Judah”: Ephraim shall not hate Judah, “and Judah shall not vex Ephraim”: Judah shall not hate the northern kingdom. Make everybody understand that. Twelve tribes.
